findings.title: Light-theme color for embedded post author links changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: The original rule for `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. It now uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original value as the light branch and uses the complement (100-X) on `$secondary` for the dark branch. Here the light-theme value changed from 30% to 70%, so these bold author names become much paler on light themes. The expected form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses 50% on `$primary` and 50% on `$secondary`, which looks copy-pasted from the adjacent `.title` rule. On light themes the member name is now lighter and no longer visually distinct from the title. The expected form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This is the same copy-paste issue as in the desktop stylesheet. The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` but the new light branch uses 50%. On light themes the name now renders the same as the title instead of darker. The expected form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length light/dark values inverted
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which looks like the arguments were swapped. On light themes the hint text becomes much darker than before, which is a regression unrelated to dark-theme support. It also disagrees with the desktop version of the same rule, which uses 70%/30%.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 light value changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The replacement uses 50% on `$primary` and 50% on `$secondary`, so on light themes the topic-map headings become noticeably lighter. The desktop counterpart keeps 20%/80%. The expected form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.
